source.prompt: open source ERP that handles production and stock management

answer.text:
**ERPNext** and **Odoo Community** are the leading open-source options for integrated production and stock management, while **Inventree** serves as a specialized lightweight alternative.

---

| System | Production Strengths | Stock Management Strengths | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ERPNext** | Multi-level Bill of Materials (BOM), Work Orders, Capacity Planning, Subcontracting | Multi-warehouse tracking, Serial/Batch tracking, Automated reorder points, Stock reconciliation | Mid-to-large businesses looking for a 100% free core ERP with full manufacturing logic |
| **Odoo Community** | Work Center routing, Manufacturing Orders, MRP schedules | Barcode integration, Double-entry inventory, Reordering rules, Multi-location tracking | Small-to-mid operations that prefer a modular UI (Note: Enterprise upgrade required for advanced MRP) |
| **InvenTree** | Light assembly tracking, BOM management, Part categorization | Serial/batch tracking, Supplier part linking, Location hierarchy, Low-stock alerts | Small teams, electronics hardware, or open-source hardware manufacturers needing stock + simple production |
| **Apache OFBiz** | Advanced MRP, Job Shop & Discrete manufacturing support | Complex multi-store tracking, Inventory valuation (FIFO/LIFO/Average Costing) | Developers or enterprise teams needing heavy customization and complex supply chains |

<Image alt="Odoo manufacturing work orders dashboard" caption="Odoo Manufacturing Interface" src="image_agent_tag_2425901768907151882"/>

---

**Key Differences to Consider**

* **ERPNext:** Completely free and open source under GNU GPLv3, including all production and inventory features out of the box.
* **Odoo:** Uses an open-core model. The Community Edition handles basic BOMs and production orders, but advanced MRP features (like Work Center capacity planning or PLM) are locked behind paid Enterprise licenses.
* **InvenTree:** Focused purely on parts inventory and simple assembly workflows, making it much easier to deploy via Docker if full ERP accounting/sales modules aren't needed.
